newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fischler plans cereals set-aside proposal in June.
newsitem.headline: Fischler plans cereals set-aside proposal in June.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler said on Tuesday that he will present a proposal in June on how much land cereals farmers must set aside for the 1998 harvest.
"We will provide a proposal at least as early as last year," Fischler told a news conference after a three-day informal meeting of EU farm ministers.
France, supported by several countries, has called for a decision before the EU summer break in August so that farmers can plan their autumn plantings.

France has called for the set-aside rate to be cut to zero from five percent, so that the EU can continue to be an active exporter in world markets. The French demand was made after a prolonged period of dry weather in Europe had threatened harvest prospects. Since then there has been widespread rain.
Fischler said it was premature to give any hint of what level of set-aside will be needed next year.
"We need a better understanding of the way things are likely to go in the cereals sector," he said.

But diplomats suggested that the set-aside rate could remain at five percent as a compromise between French demands and those of Germany which favours as high a rate as possible. -Peter Blackburn, Middelburg press centre +31 118 650 679
